full_judgment: 3. The defendant Nos. 1 and 2 entered appearance upon filing written statement denying the material allegations made in I the plaint contending inter alia that there is no cause of action in the suit and the same is barred by limitation as also it is barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. It is also stated in the written statement that the suit land appertains to Khatian No. 438 covering an area of 1.02 acres originally belonged to Hamid Ali and Rowshan Ali. Upon an amicable partition Hamid Ali obtained .51 decimals from the western part of the suit plot. Thereafter, he mortgaged .51 decimals of land to Arob Ali, the predecessor in interest of the defendants on 15 April, 1966. Thereafter, the said land was purchased by Arob Ali from Hamid Ali and the said purchase deed was registered under section 75 of the Registration Act on 24.12.1969. Arbo Ali having been in possession of the suit land died leaving behind two sons, i.e. defendant Nos. 1 and 2 and three daughters namely, Rejia Begum, Afruza Begum, Lili Begum and one wife Doulatunnessa. In the written statement the defendants also made an averment that the said original purchase deed dated 24.12.1969 was lost in the year of 1971. It is also disclosed in their written statement that they have been possessing the suit land through one Nuruzzaman a caretaker under them and they have also mutated their names in the record of right in respect of the suit land vide Mutation Case No. 4621 of 1998-99; the plaintiff has got no right, title, interest and possession over the suit land and the suit has been instituted on the basis of some forged documents.
